names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 13 mai, «Sfântul Cuvios Eftimie Ivirul».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Μαΐου, «Όσιος Ευθύμιος ο Νέος κτήτορας της Μονής Ιβήρων Αγίου Όρους», with the rank word, the epithet and the house left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's third heading for the Julian 13 May, „Преподобни Јован, Јевтимије Георгије и Гаврил Иверски.“ — Преподобни left off, which is the `venerable` this folder already carries in `types`, and **Иверски kept**, which is not a rank but the epithet "the Iberian" the heading sets after all four names and which the entry's first sentence confirms belongs to all four. Measured: a bare «Јевтимије» would fold with `euthymius-of-dimitsana`, where this form folds with nothing. The body spells his name Јефтимије in its second sentence and Јевтимије in the heading and the third; **the heading's spelling is what is stored**, and the book's own variation is recorded here rather than corrected. The translation of the Scriptures and the 1028 are in the body.

Read out of the heading of days.pravoslavie.ru's name link 739, «Евфимий Новый, Святогорец, Иверский (Афонский), прп.», with the rank word left off. The calendar gives him three epithets at once and a parenthetical alternate for the second, and the day line puts Иверский first — «Прп. Евфимия Иверского, Святогорца (1028) (Груз.).» — so that is the pair stored, and Новый, Святогорец and Афонский are recorded here. `fk.mjs` was run on «Евфимий Иверский», «Евфимий Новый» and «Евфимий Новый Святогорец» and returned NONE for all three.

death.note: The title of doxologia.ro's page for him: «Viața Cuviosului Eftimie Ivirul (†1028)». The body of the page gives no year of death.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 13 мая ст. ст. — «Прп. Евфимия Иверского, Святогорца (1028) (Груз.).»

attestations.note: The same menologion day the folder already keeps for the other three churches, the same year, 1028, and the same man: the Georgian who translated the Scriptures and the service books into Georgian at the Iveron his father founded. The Russian marks him «(Груз.)», a saint of the Georgian church, which is how this source flags an entry it keeps from another local church. **His life page lists three days — «Дни памяти: 13 мая , 1 июня (Афон.) , 12 июля» — and only the first is the day page that printed him**, so the other two are recorded here as a note and not as a feast, per BRIEF.md §8; the 1 июня is marked as the Athonite synaxis and the 12 июля is the day the same page gives his father. **`dates` were not touched.** The folder carries 1028 off doxologia's title and the Russian day line gives the same year; the Russian adds «на 65 году жизни», in the sixty-fifth year of his life, which subtracted from 1028 would give a birth about 963 — **a lifespan taken off a death is a calculation and not a year any book prints**, so no birth was recorded, which is the refusal `rostislav-of-great-moravia` and `epiphanius-of-cyprus` already carry. The day page prints hymns for three of the saints it heads and nothing under his name. azbyka.ru was not read.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 13 mai — «Sfântul Cuvios Eftimie Ivirul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Ευθύμιος ο Νέος κτήτορας της Μονής Ιβήρων Αγίου Όρους»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar already keeps him on, and it is plainly the same man: the son of John Varasvatse, second abbot of Iviron, and the page says he died on 13 May. **He is none of the corpus's twenty-odd other Euthymii**, which the namesweep flagged and which were read. **The Greek dates his death to 1028 at Constantinople** — «Το 1028 μ.Χ. πήγε στην Κωνσταντινούπολη για Αγιορείτικες υποθέσεις, όπου και πέθανε στις 13 Μαΐου» — with the head line «(; - 1028)», and the existing `dates` object is **not** touched; the year is recorded here and in the added paragraph so a later reader can lift it with this citation. **It names his birthplace**, the city of Tao in Iberia, which the corpus may not hold. **Three men are linked and one is not**: his father [John the Iberian](/saints/john-the-iberian) and [Athanasius the Athonite](/saints/athanasius-the-athonite), by whose Lavra the Georgians first settled, both have folders; Basil II, with whose help Iviron was founded and who offered Euthymius the archbishopric of Cyprus, has none. No hymn is printed.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 26.05.2026 (13. мај ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Јован, Јевтимије Георгије и Гаврил Иверски.“

attestations.note: The day's third entry, an enumerated company of four, so one row each, on the same menologion day the Romanian and the Greek keep all four on, so nothing moved. **THE 1028 AGREES EXACTLY AND NOTHING IN `dates` WAS TOUCHED**: „Јевтимије се упокојио 1028.“ is the year this folder already holds off the title of doxologia's page, «Viața Cuviosului Eftimie Ivirul (†1028)», whose body gave none — so a year that stood on a page title alone now has a second book behind it. **New here**: that **he and George translated the Holy Scriptures into the Georgian tongue**, which is the plainest statement of what he did that this folder holds and is what its `hymnographer` type stands beside. **`related_add: ["gabriel-the-iberian"]`**, the one of the four this folder did not carry; the reciprocal is in the same file. `types` untouched: Преподобни is the `venerable` the folder carries. **No `locations`**. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
